title: Act Done by Person Bound, or by Mistake of Fact Believing Bound, by Law
old_text: Nothing is an offence which is done by a person who is, or who by reason of a mistake of fact and not by reason of a mistake of law in good faith believes himself to be, bound by law to do it.
new_text: Nothing is an offence which is done by a person who is, or who by reason of a mistake of fact and not by reason of a mistake of law in good faith believes himself to be, bound by law to do it.
punishment_old: Complete statutory general defence.
punishment_new: Complete statutory general defence.
explanation: IPC Section 76 is renumbered as BNS Section 14. It codifies the principle that an honest mistake of fact (not law) made in good faith excludes criminal liability when the person believes they are bound by law.

title: Act of Judge When Acting Judicially
old_text: Nothing is an offence which is done by a Judge when acting judicially in the exercise of any power which is, or which in good faith he believes to be, given to him by law.
new_text: Nothing is an offence which is done by a Judge when acting judicially in the exercise of any power which is, or which in good faith he believes to be, given to him by law.
punishment_old: Judicial immunity from criminal prosecution.
punishment_new: Judicial immunity from criminal prosecution.
explanation: IPC Section 77 is renumbered as Section 15 of BNS. It affords absolute criminal immunity to judges performing judicial duties in good faith.

title: Act Done Pursuant to Judgment or Order of Court
old_text: Nothing which is done in pursuance of, or which is warranted by the judgment or order of, a Court, if done whilst such judgment or order remains in force, is an offence, notwithstanding the Court had no jurisdiction.
new_text: Nothing which is done in pursuance of, or which is warranted by the judgment or order of, a Court, if done whilst such judgment or order remains in force, is an offence, notwithstanding the Court had no jurisdiction.
punishment_old: Protection for ministerial officers executing court warrants.
punishment_new: Protection for ministerial officers executing court warrants.
explanation: IPC Section 78 is renumbered as BNS Section 16. It shields court officers (such as executioners or bailiffs) who execute court orders in good faith even if the court lacked jurisdiction.

title: Act Done by Person Justified, or by Mistake of Fact Believing Justified, by Law
old_text: Nothing is an offence which is done by any person who is justified by law, or who by reason of a mistake of fact and not by reason of a mistake of law in good faith, believes himself to be justified by law, in doing it.
new_text: Nothing is an offence which is done by any person who is justified by law, or who by reason of a mistake of fact and not by reason of a mistake of law in good faith, believes himself to be justified by law, in doing it.
punishment_old: Complete statutory general defence.
punishment_new: Complete statutory general defence.
explanation: IPC Section 79 is renumbered as BNS Section 17. It protects individuals who act under a bona fide mistake of fact believing their conduct to be justified by law, such as a citizen seizing a suspected murderer.

title: Accident in Doing a Lawful Act
old_text: Nothing is an offence which is done by accident or misfortune, and without any criminal intention or knowledge in the doing of a lawful act in a lawful manner by lawful means and with proper care and caution.
new_text: Nothing is an offence which is done by accident or misfortune, and without any criminal intention or knowledge in the doing of a lawful act in a lawful manner by lawful means and with proper care and caution.
punishment_old: Complete defence of inevitable accident.
punishment_new: Complete defence of inevitable accident.
explanation: IPC Section 80 is renumbered as Section 18 of BNS. It excuses harm resulting from an accident provided the underlying act was lawful and executed with proper care and caution.

title: Act Likely to Cause Harm, Done Without Criminal Intent, to Prevent Other Harm
old_text: Nothing is an offence merely by reason of its being done with the knowledge that it is likely to cause harm, if it be done without any criminal intention to cause harm, and in good faith for the purpose of preventing or avoiding other harm to person or property.
new_text: Nothing is an offence merely by reason of its being done with the knowledge that it is likely to cause harm, if it be done without any criminal intention to cause harm, and in good faith for the purpose of preventing or avoiding other harm to person or property.
punishment_old: Doctrine of necessity defence.
punishment_new: Doctrine of necessity defence.
explanation: IPC Section 81 is renumbered as BNS Section 19. It enshrines the doctrine of necessity, justifying causing lesser harm in good faith to prevent a greater disaster.

title: Act of Child Under Seven Years of Age
old_text: Nothing is an offence which is done by a child under seven years of age.
new_text: Nothing is an offence which is done by a child under seven years of age.
punishment_old: Absolute legal incapacity (doli incapax).
punishment_new: Absolute legal incapacity (doli incapax).
explanation: IPC Section 82 is renumbered as BNS Section 20. It provides an irrebuttable statutory presumption that a child under seven years of age cannot form criminal intent.

title: Act of Child Above Seven and Under Twelve of Immature Understanding
old_text: Nothing is an offence which is done by a child above seven years of age and under twelve, who has not attained sufficient maturity of understanding to judge of the nature and consequences of his conduct on that occasion.
new_text: Nothing is an offence which is done by a child above seven years of age and under twelve, who has not attained sufficient maturity of understanding to judge of the nature and consequences of his conduct on that occasion.
punishment_old: Qualified immunity based on lack of maturity.
punishment_new: Qualified immunity based on lack of maturity.
explanation: IPC Section 83 is renumbered as Section 21 of BNS. It grants rebuttable immunity to children aged between 7 and 12 who lack the maturity to understand the nature of their actions.

title: Act of a Person of Unsound Mind
old_text: Nothing is an offence which is done by a person who, at the time of doing it, by reason of unsoundness of mind, is incapable of knowing the nature of the act, or that he is doing what is either wrong or contrary to law.
new_text: Nothing is an offence which is done by a person who, at the time of doing it, by reason of unsoundness of mind, is incapable of knowing the nature of the act, or that he is doing what is either wrong or contrary to law.
punishment_old: Complete statutory insanity defence (McNaghten rule).
punishment_new: Complete statutory insanity defence (McNaghten rule).
explanation: IPC Section 84 is renumbered as BNS Section 22. It retains the McNaghten legal insanity defence, requiring proof that unsoundness of mind incapacitated the accused from knowing the act was wrong or contrary to law.

title: Involuntary Intoxication Causing Incapacity of Judgment
old_text: Nothing is an offence which is done by a person who, at the time of doing it, is, by reason of intoxication, incapable of knowing the nature of the act, or that he is doing what is either wrong, or contrary to law: provided that the thing which intoxicated him was administered to him without his knowledge or against his will.
new_text: Nothing is an offence which is done by a person who, at the time of doing it, is, by reason of intoxication, incapable of knowing the nature of the act, or that he is doing what is either wrong, or contrary to law: provided that the thing which intoxicated him was administered to him without his knowledge or against his will.
punishment_old: Complete defence for involuntary intoxication.
punishment_new: Complete defence for involuntary intoxication.
explanation: IPC Section 85 is renumbered as BNS Section 23. It protects individuals whose judgment is impaired by substances administered without their knowledge or against their will.

title: Offence Requiring Particular Intent or Knowledge by Intoxicated Person
old_text: In cases where an act is not an offence unless done with a particular knowledge or intent, a person who does the act in a state of intoxication shall be liable to be dealt with as if he had the same knowledge as he would have had if he had not been intoxicated, unless intoxicated against his will.
new_text: In cases where an act is not an offence unless done with a particular knowledge or intent, a person who does the act in a state of intoxication shall be liable to be dealt with as if he had the same knowledge as he would have had if he had not been intoxicated, unless intoxicated against his will.
punishment_old: Presumption of knowledge despite voluntary intoxication.
punishment_new: Presumption of knowledge despite voluntary intoxication.
explanation: IPC Section 86 is renumbered as Section 24 of BNS. It establishes that voluntary drunkenness does not negate statutory knowledge, treating the offender as if sober regarding legal awareness.

title: Act Done by Consent Not Intended to Cause Death or Grievous Hurt
old_text: Nothing which is not intended to cause death, or grievous hurt, and which is not known by the doer to be likely to cause death or grievous hurt, is an offence by reason of any harm which it may cause, or be intended by the doer to cause, to any person, above eighteen years of age, who has given consent.
new_text: Nothing which is not intended to cause death, or grievous hurt, and which is not known by the doer to be likely to cause death or grievous hurt, is an offence by reason of any harm which it may cause, or be intended by the doer to cause, to any person, above eighteen years of age, who has given consent.
punishment_old: Volenti non fit injuria defence (sports, games).
punishment_new: Volenti non fit injuria defence (sports, games).
explanation: IPC Section 87 is renumbered as BNS Section 25. It codifies consent for lawful competitive sports (like boxing or cricket) between adults where death or grievous hurt is not intended.

title: Act Done in Good Faith for Person's Benefit with Consent
old_text: Nothing, which is not intended to cause death, is an offence by reason of any harm which it may cause, or be intended by the doer to cause, or be known by the doer to be likely to cause, to any person for whose benefit it is done in good faith, and who has given a consent.
new_text: Nothing, which is not intended to cause death, is an offence by reason of any harm which it may cause, or be intended by the doer to cause, or be known by the doer to be likely to cause, to any person for whose benefit it is done in good faith, and who has given a consent.
punishment_old: Medical and surgical operation exception with consent.
punishment_new: Medical and surgical operation exception with consent.
explanation: IPC Section 88 is renumbered as BNS Section 26. It protects surgeons and medical practitioners performing dangerous operations in good faith for a patient's benefit with consent.

title: Act Done in Good Faith for Benefit of Child or Person of Unsound Mind by Guardian
old_text: Nothing which is done in good faith for the benefit of a person under twelve years of age, or of unsound mind, by or by consent, either express or implied, of the guardian or other person having lawful charge of that person, is an offence by reason of any harm which it may cause.
new_text: Nothing which is done in good faith for the benefit of a person under twelve years of age, or of unsound mind, by or by consent, either express or implied, of the guardian or other person having lawful charge of that person, is an offence by reason of any harm which it may cause.
punishment_old: Guardian consent exception.
punishment_new: Guardian consent exception.
explanation: IPC Section 89 is renumbered as Section 27 of BNS. It allows parents or legal guardians to give valid consent for beneficial medical treatment of young children or mentally infirm wards.

title: Consent Known to be Given Under Fear or Misconception
old_text: A consent is not such a consent as it intended by any section of this Code, if the consent is given by a person under fear of injury, or under a misconception of fact, or by person of unsound mind, or by a child under twelve years of age.
new_text: A consent is not such a consent as is intended by any section of this Sanhita, if the consent is given by a person under fear of injury, or under a misconception of fact, or by person of unsound mind, or by a child under twelve years of age.
punishment_old: Invalidates vitiated consent.
punishment_new: Invalidates vitiated consent.
explanation: IPC Section 90 is renumbered as BNS Section 28. It specifies that consent extracted through coercion, threat, intoxication, or misconception of fact is legally void.

title: Exclusion of Acts Which are Offences Independently of Harm Caused
old_text: The exceptions in sections 87, 88 and 89 do not extend to acts which are offences independently of any harm which they may cause, or be intended to cause, or be known to be likely to cause, to the person giving the consent, or on whose behalf the consent is given.
new_text: The exceptions in sections 25, 26 and 27 do not extend to acts which are offences independently of any harm which they may cause, or be intended to cause, or be known to be likely to cause, to the person giving the consent, or on whose behalf the consent is given.
punishment_old: Consent cannot legalize an inherently illegal act (e.g., miscarriage).
punishment_new: Consent cannot legalize an inherently illegal act.
explanation: IPC Section 91 is renumbered as Section 29 of BNS. It clarifies that consent cannot legalize acts that are independently prohibited by law, such as unlawful termination of pregnancy.

title: Act Done in Good Faith for Benefit of Person Without Consent
old_text: Nothing is an offence by reason of any harm which it may cause to a person for whose benefit it is done in good faith, even without that person's consent, if the circumstances are such that it is impossible for that person to signify consent.
new_text: Nothing is an offence by reason of any harm which it may cause to a person for whose benefit it is done in good faith, even without that person's consent, if the circumstances are such that it is impossible for that person to signify consent.
punishment_old: Emergency medical treatment exception without consent.
punishment_new: Emergency medical treatment exception without consent.
explanation: IPC Section 92 is renumbered as Section 30 of BNS. It protects emergency medical interventions, such as surgery on an unconscious accident victim where obtaining consent is impossible.

title: Communication Made in Good Faith
old_text: No communication made in good faith is an offence by reason of any harm to the person to whom it is made, if it is made for the benefit of that person.
new_text: No communication made in good faith is an offence by reason of any harm to the person to whom it is made, if it is made for the benefit of that person.
punishment_old: Doctor-patient communication protection.
punishment_new: Doctor-patient communication protection.
explanation: IPC Section 93 is renumbered as Section 31 of BNS. It shields doctors who disclose grave medical diagnoses to patients in good faith, even if the shock causes subsequent injury.

title: Act to Which Person is Compelled by Threats (Duress)
old_text: Except murder, and offences against the State punishable with death, nothing is an offence which is done by a person who is compelled to do it by threats, which, at the time of doing it, reasonably cause the apprehension that instant death to that person will otherwise be the consequence.
new_text: Except murder, and offences against the State punishable with death, nothing is an offence which is done by a person who is compelled to do it by threats, which, at the time of doing it, reasonably cause the apprehension that instant death to that person will otherwise be the consequence.
punishment_old: Defence of duress (excluding murder and treason).
punishment_new: Defence of duress (excluding murder and treason).
explanation: IPC Section 94 is renumbered as Section 32 of BNS. It codifies the defence of duress where a person acts under threat of instant death, but expressly excludes murder and capital treason.

title: Act Causing Slight Harm (De Minimis Rule)
old_text: Nothing is an offence by reason that it causes, or that it is intended to cause, or that it is known to be likely to cause, any harm, if that harm is so slight that no person of ordinary sense and temper would complain of such harm.
new_text: Nothing is an offence by reason that it causes, or that it is intended to cause, or that it is known to be likely to cause, any harm, if that harm is so slight that no person of ordinary sense and temper would complain of such harm.
punishment_old: De minimis non curat lex rule.
punishment_new: De minimis non curat lex rule.
explanation: IPC Section 95 is renumbered as BNS Section 33. It embodies the ancient maxim 'de minimis non curat lex' (the law does not care for trifles), preventing prosecution for trivial friction in everyday life.

title: Things Done in Private Defence
old_text: Nothing is an offence which is done in the exercise of the right of private defence.
new_text: Nothing is an offence which is done in the exercise of the right of private defence.
punishment_old: General declaration of right of private defence.
punishment_new: General declaration of right of private defence.
explanation: IPC Section 96 is renumbered as Section 34 of BNS. It opens the private defence sub-chapter by establishing that justifiable self-defence excludes criminal culpability entirely.

title: Right of Private Defence of Body and Property
old_text: Every person has a right, subject to the restrictions contained in section 99, to defend: First—His own body, and the body of any other person, against any offence affecting the human body; Secondly—The property, whether movable or immovable, of himself or of any other person, against theft, robbery, mischief or criminal trespass.
new_text: Every person has a right, subject to the restrictions contained in section 37, to defend his own body and the body of any other person against offences affecting the body; and property against theft, robbery, mischief or criminal trespass.
punishment_old: Scope of defence of person and property.
punishment_new: Scope of defence of person and property.
explanation: IPC Section 97 is renumbered as Section 35 of BNS. It recognizes the fundamental right to defend not only one's own body and property, but also the body and property of any other person.

title: Right of Private Defence Against Act of Person of Unsound Mind or Child
old_text: When an act, which would otherwise be a certain offence, is not that offence, by reason of the youth, the want of maturity of understanding, the unsoundness of mind or the intoxication of the person doing it, every person has the same right of private defence as if the act were that offence.
new_text: When an act, which would otherwise be a certain offence, is not that offence, by reason of the youth, the want of maturity of understanding, the unsoundness of mind or the intoxication of the person doing it, every person has the same right of private defence as if the act were that offence.
punishment_old: Self-defence permitted against legally immune attackers.
punishment_new: Self-defence permitted against legally immune attackers.
explanation: IPC Section 98 is renumbered as Section 36 of BNS. It confirms that the right of self-defence remains available against attacks by children, insane individuals, or intoxicated persons, even though they lack criminal capacity.

title: Acts Against Which There is No Right of Private Defence
old_text: There is no right of private defence against an act which does not reasonably cause the apprehension of death or grievous hurt, if done, or attempted to be done, by a public servant acting in good faith under colour of his office; nor when there is time to have recourse to the protection of public authorities; and the right in no case extends to inflicting more harm than it is necessary to inflict for the purpose of defence.
new_text: There is no right of private defence against an act which does not reasonably cause the apprehension of death or grievous hurt, if done, or attempted to be done, by a public servant acting in good faith under colour of his office; nor when there is time to have recourse to the protection of public authorities; and the right in no case extends to inflicting more harm than it is necessary to inflict for the purpose of defence.
punishment_old: Statutory limitations on private defence (proportionality & recourse).
punishment_new: Statutory limitations on private defence (proportionality & recourse).
explanation: IPC Section 99 is renumbered as Section 37 of BNS. It imposes key boundaries: no defence against good-faith public servant actions lacking deadly threat, mandatory recourse to authorities when feasible, and strict proportionality in harm inflicted.

title: When Right of Private Defence of Body Extends to Causing Death
old_text: The right of private defence of the body extends to the voluntary causing of death if the offence occasions reasonable apprehension of death, grievous hurt, rape, gratifying unnatural lust, kidnapping/abduction, wrongful confinement, or acid throwing.
new_text: The right of private defence of the body extends, under the restrictions mentioned in section 37, to the voluntary causing of death, or of any other harm to the assailant, if the offence which occasions the exercise of the right be of any of the seven specified deadly categories.
punishment_old: Justification for causing death of assailant.
punishment_new: Justification for causing death of assailant.
explanation: IPC Section 100 is renumbered as Section 38 of BNS. It lists the seven grave situations (including threats of death, grievous hurt, rape, abduction, and acid attack) where an individual may lawfully cause the death of an assailant in self-defence.

title: When Right Extends to Causing Any Harm Other Than Death
old_text: If the offence be not of any of the descriptions enumerated in the last preceding section, the right of private defence of the body does not extend to the voluntary causing of death to the assailant, but does extend, subject to restrictions, to the voluntary causing of any harm other than death.
new_text: If the offence be not of any of the descriptions enumerated in the last preceding section, the right of private defence of the body does not extend to the voluntary causing of death to the assailant, but does extend, subject to restrictions, to the voluntary causing of any harm other than death.
punishment_old: Harm short of death justified for lesser bodily attacks.
punishment_new: Harm short of death justified for lesser bodily attacks.
explanation: IPC Section 101 is renumbered as Section 39 of BNS. For bodily assaults not falling within the seven deadly categories of Section 38, self-defence justifies causing harm short of death.

title: Commencement and Continuance of Right of Private Defence of Body
old_text: The right of private defence of the body commences as soon as a reasonable apprehension of danger to the body arises from an attempt or threat to commit the offence, though the offence may not have been committed; and it continues as long as such apprehension of danger to the body continues.
new_text: The right of private defence of the body commences as soon as a reasonable apprehension of danger to the body arises from an attempt or threat to commit the offence, though the offence may not have been committed; and it continues as long as such apprehension of danger to the body continues.
punishment_old: Duration governed by reasonable apprehension of bodily danger.
punishment_new: Duration governed by reasonable apprehension of bodily danger.
explanation: IPC Section 102 is renumbered as BNS Section 40. It defines the temporal span of self-defence: it begins the moment a reasonable apprehension of danger arises and ends when the danger ceases.

title: When Right of Private Defence of Property Extends to Causing Death
old_text: The right of private defence of property extends to voluntary causing of death if the offence be robbery, house-breaking by night, mischief by fire to building/vessel, or theft/mischief/trespass causing reasonable apprehension of death or grievous hurt.
new_text: The right of private defence of property extends, under restrictions in section 37, to voluntary causing of death or other harm to the wrong-doer, if the offence be robbery, house-breaking by night, mischief by fire or explosive substance, or property offences causing apprehension of death/grievous hurt.
punishment_old: Justification for causing death in extreme property attacks.
punishment_new: Justification for causing death in extreme property attacks.
explanation: IPC Section 103 is renumbered as Section 41 of BNS. It allows an owner or defender to cause death in defence of property during robbery, nocturnal housebreaking, arson, or deadly trespass.

title: When Right Extends to Causing Any Harm Other Than Death to Property Offender
old_text: If the offence the committing of which, or the attempting to commit which, occasions the exercise of the right of private defence, be theft, mischief, or criminal trespass, not of any of the descriptions enumerated in the last preceding section, that right does not extend to the voluntary causing of death, but does extend to any harm other than death.
new_text: If the offence the committing of which, or the attempting to commit which, occasions the exercise of the right of private defence, be theft, mischief, or criminal trespass, not of any of the descriptions enumerated in the last preceding section, that right does not extend to the voluntary causing of death, but does extend to any harm other than death.
punishment_old: Harm other than death for ordinary property offences.
punishment_new: Harm other than death for ordinary property offences.
explanation: IPC Section 104 is renumbered as Section 42 of BNS. For standard property offences like simple daytime theft or mischief, the defender may use proportionate physical force short of lethal harm.

title: Commencement and Continuance of Right of Private Defence of Property
old_text: Right commences when reasonable apprehension of danger to property commences. In theft, continues till offender has effected retreat with property, or assistance obtained, or property recovered. In robbery, continues during offender causing/attempting death/hurt. In trespass/mischief, continues as long as trespass/mischief continues.
new_text: Right commences when reasonable apprehension of danger to property commences. In theft, continues till offender retreats with property, or assistance obtained, or property recovered. In robbery, continues during offender causing/attempting death/hurt. In trespass/mischief, continues as long as trespass/mischief continues.
punishment_old: Duration rules for property defence.
punishment_new: Duration rules for property defence.
explanation: IPC Section 105 is renumbered as BNS Section 43. It sets out the exact points in time when the right of property defence begins and terminates for theft, robbery, criminal trespass, and night housebreaking.

title: Right of Private Defence Against Deadly Assault When Risk of Harm to Innocent Person
old_text: If in the exercise of the right of private defence against an assault which reasonably causes the apprehension of death, the defender be so situated that he cannot effectually exercise that right without risk of harm to an innocent person, his right of private defence extends to the running of that risk.
new_text: If in the exercise of the right of private defence against an assault which reasonably causes the apprehension of death, the defender be so situated that he cannot effectually exercise that right without risk of harm to an innocent person, his right of private defence extends to the running of that risk.
punishment_old: Harm to innocent bystander excused during deadly assault.
punishment_new: Harm to innocent bystander excused during deadly assault.
explanation: IPC Section 106 is renumbered as BNS Section 44. When a person facing a lethal mob attack must fire to defend their life, the incidental risk of injuring innocent bystanders in the crowd is excused.
